coverageAudit.label: Exercise 1
coverageAudit.note: Null-set deletion preserves measure; indicator integrals or disjoint additivity provide the argument.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 2
coverageAudit.note: Explicit negative travelling-mass counterexample.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 3
coverageAudit.note: Both directions of the indicator measurability test.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 4
coverageAudit.note: One common exceptional set preserves the nonnegative limit.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 5
coverageAudit.note: DCT gives the useful bounded-E strengthening; printed arbitrary-E statement is trivial.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 6
coverageAudit.note: Granular methods cover the eight parameter variations: pointwise limits, rescaling, integral finiteness, and moving maxima; no separate card per arithmetic variant.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 7
coverageAudit.note: General target-exponent product inequality.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 8
coverageAudit.note: Near-zero and tail radial powers, with p∞ handled separately.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 9
coverageAudit.note: All six variants use endpoint asymptotics; critical power-log and essential boundedness tests supplied.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 10
coverageAudit.note: Six variants share scaling, dominated convergence, and membership checks; explicit non-L2 example and exponential threshold included.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 11
coverageAudit.note: Printed central value n contradicts advertised finite-p convergence; analyzed literally and flagged.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 12
coverageAudit.note: Young plus kernel translation continuity and local KRF.

coverageAudit.label: Exercise 13
coverageAudit.note: Requires nonzero compact bump; drift defeats global compactness despite translation control.

notes.coverage: Archived additions without a verified current lecture reference remain ahead. Material matched to the 28 October transcription is current, with the archive retained as a secondary reference.
notes.sectionNumbers: New app group numbers3.9–3.14 are navigation identifiers, not archived subsection numbering; archiveReference.section carries the original subsection.
notes.proofs: All proof sketches are added study explanations. Archive omissions and corrections are stated explicitly.
sourceErrors: The archive states existence and names Vitali, without providing a construction or proof. This proof sketch is added study material, not a lecture or archive quotation.
The archive proof on p78 says x∈K implies d(x,K)=1; the correct distance is zero. The displayed ratio cutoff still has value one. This card uses the equivalent simpler distance cutoff.
A diagonal sequence requires coordinated approximations; the sketch uses one explicit truncation/quantization schedule rather than assuming an arbitrary diagonal converges.
For signed coefficients the error bound is |α|ᵖm(U\K), not αᵖm(U\K). Choose U inside Ω so the resulting support is compact in the required domain.

The archive argument choosing any function discontinuous at one point is insufficient: changing a continuous function at one point does not change its L∞ class. The counterexample here has a genuine essential jump. Empty domains are excluded.
The archive omits the finite-p proof and sketches the rational-box approximation route. The proof sketch expands that route.
The conclusion needs a nontrivial domain. On a null domain L∞ consists only of the zero class and is separable; the archive’s surrounding setting is an open domain.
The archive proves p=1 and treats∞ directly, but omits the interior-p proof. That proof is supplied here as a study sketch.
The card uses the real bilinear pairing as in the archive. A complex sesquilinear pairing requires the corresponding conjugation.

The archive omits the closure in the general statement. Sums of two arbitrary closed sets need not be closed; the proof only gives the closed-sum inclusion. Compactly supported applications in the following pages are unaffected.

The codomain includes zero; a constant function contradicts the archive’s strictly positive codomain. Use a slightly smaller δ when passing from a strict-distance uniform-continuity condition to |x−y|≤δ.
The archive says multi-index length “less than k”; the same proof gives the usual |α|≤k conclusion. The difference quotient denominator is |h|, not the vector h.
Visually checked p85: the archive’s bump example has the impossible condition |x|<0. The intended condition is |x|<1. Its support condition uses the closed ball.
Uniform continuity must be applied on a compact enlargement, since x−y need not remain in K. The conclusion is on each fixed compact set, not necessarily uniform on all of space.
The archive omits the general-domain details. The sketch supplies a compact-support-first argument that avoids mollifying across the boundary.
The conclusion from zero integral is zero almost everywhere, not pointwise. The archive’s phrase “identically zero” should be read in this a.e. sense.
Individual translation continuity is the standard density-based step used in the archived convolution compactness exercise; this proof is supplied as study material.

The archive applies Arzelà–Ascoli to a merely bounded measurable set ω. The sketch applies it on a compact containing ball, then restricts. Finite measure is used in the tail reduction; Ω itself need not be bounded.
The archive states this sufficient global criterion and omits proof. The sketch gives the local-to-global argument; it does not attribute a proof to the archive.
Exercise 13 requires a nonzero bump; the zero bump gives a compact singleton. Use translations along a fixed coordinate direction in dimensions greater than one.

The printed exercise merely asks for a measurable E, which is trivial with E=ℝᵈ. Its DCT hint indicates the useful stronger bounded-set conclusion; the card states and proves that strengthening explicitly.
The printed power inequalities are finite-p criteria. They must not be applied literally at p=∞.

Visually checked pp92–93: the central value is printed n, while the exercise claims finite-p convergence. These are inconsistent. The card analyzes the printed formula and does not silently substitute a guessed intended formula such as nx.
